# pping

## Maturity

**Grade:** 2 · limited by scope (core), evidence (oracle MIXED) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — pollere/pping TCP-timestamp technique, one flow per estimator (surveyed 2026-09-30; re-assessed 2026-10-06 against that survey, no new survey: mvp -> core after ICMP/ICMPv6 echo RTT matching landed)

**Audit:** review 2026-07-19 · mutation 2026-08-13

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

**Passive RTT estimation with zero active probing.** An observation point that
can see both directions of a TCP flow — a tap, a router, a middlebox; anything
that is not an endpoint — recovers the round-trip time from the flow's own
RFC 7323 TCP Timestamps option. Every segment carrying the option asserts a
TSval ("my clock reads this now") and echoes a TSecr ("the last TSval I validly
received from you"). Because a TSecr is only ever a TSval the *other* side
actually sent, matching a TSecr seen going one way back to the TSval that
produced it — seen going the other way, earlier — is exactly the elapsed round
trip. No cooperation from either endpoint, and not one synthetic byte on the
wire.

**Ping traffic too.** The same bounded table pairs an ICMP Echo Request
(type 8) or ICMPv6 Echo Request (128) with the Echo Reply (0 / 129) that
carries the same identifier and sequence number back the other way, so the
ping traffic crossing a router is measured as well. Samples come out as the
same `RttSample`, tagged with which rule produced them.

- **Status:** the core scope is implemented — TCP Timestamps and ICMP / ICMPv6
  Echo, one flow per estimator: both decoders, the bounded table, and both
  matching rules. QUIC spin bit and a multi-flow table are under
  [Backlog / deferred](#backlog--deferred).
  **Platform:** any — no sockets, no wall-clock read; `now` is caller-supplied.
- **Deps:** none (std only).
- **Model after:** Kathleen Nichols' *pping* (Pollere LLC) passive-RTT
  technique, over RFC 7323 TSval/TSecr; echo matching over RFC 792 / RFC 4443
  identifier and sequence, as xdp-project's pping also does.

## The algorithm

- Per flow, per direction, a bounded table maps `tsval -> first_seen_time`,
  storing only the **first** time each distinct TSval was seen that way.
- A packet going the **opposite** direction carrying `tsecr = T` matches the
  entry for `tsval == T` in the opposite direction's table, and emits
  `now - stored_time`.
- **First-echo-only.** A match *consumes* the entry rather than reading it. A
  later segment re-echoing the same TSecr — a delayed ACK, a duplicate ACK from
  loss or reordering, a keepalive — finds nothing and correctly produces no
  second, inflated sample. Without this rule every duplicate echo would
  masquerade as a fresh (and wrong) measurement.
- **Bounded memory.** Fixed `capacity` per (flow, direction), allocated once and
  never grown, plus `max_age` eviction: a TSval nobody echoes within a few
  worst-case RTTs is never coming back.
- Matching is **exact 32-bit equality**, which is what makes the scheme agnostic
  to each host's TSval tick rate (RFC 7323 §5.3 leaves it host-specific) and
  immune to the wraparound reasoning an ordering-based comparison would need.

### ICMP / ICMPv6 Echo

- The table key is `identifier << 16 | sequence` (`IcmpEcho.key`). An **Echo
  Request** going direction *d* is stored in *d*'s table, first-seen only (a
  duplicated request keeps its first time). It never matches anything.
- An **Echo Reply** going the opposite way with the same key consumes the
  entry and emits `now - stored_time`, tagged `.icmp_echo` or `.icmpv6_echo`.
  A duplicate reply (ping's `DUP!`) finds nothing; an unmatched reply emits
  nothing and stores nothing.
- Same exact-equality rule, so the 16-bit sequence wrapping from 65535 to 0 is
  just another key; same `capacity` and `max_age` eviction.
- **One estimator is one kind of traffic.** TSvals and echo keys are both
  `u32` and would collide in one table, so the first `observe` or
  `observeEcho` after `init`/`reset` fixes `Estimator.traffic`; a call of the
  other kind afterwards returns `null`, touches no table and counts in
  `observations_refused`. A ping flow is its own flow.
- Checksums are not verified (a snaplen-cut capture cannot, and the endpoints
  already did); a corrupted packet costs at most one wrong or missing sample.

## Use

```zig
const pping = @import("pping");

var est = try pping.Estimator.init(gpa, .{ .capacity = 256, .max_age = 60_000 });
defer est.deinit(gpa);

const ts = pping.parseTcpTimestamps(tcp_options_bytes) orelse return;
if (est.observe(.{ .dir = .a_to_b, .tsval = ts.tsval, .tsecr = ts.tsecr, .now = t })) |s| {
    // s.rtt, in whatever unit `now` is in — this module never picks one.
}
```

Ping traffic, from whole IP packets (no link-layer header):

```zig
// One Estimator per unordered address pair {src, dst}, in the caller's map.
const e = (pping.parseIpEcho(ip_packet) catch return) orelse return; // not an echo
const est: *pping.Estimator = flows.get(e.src, e.dst); // caller-side demultiplexing
if (est.observeEcho(.{ .dir = e.direction(), .echo = e.echo, .now = t })) |s| {
    // s.proto == .icmp_echo or .icmpv6_echo
    // s.echoIdentifier(), s.echoSequence(), s.rtt
}
```

| API | What it does |
|---|---|
| `parseIpEcho(packet) EchoParseError!?IpEcho` | IPv4 (IHL, total length, first fragment only) or IPv6 (Hop-by-Hop, Routing, Destination Options, Fragment, AH; at most `max_ipv6_extension_headers` = 8) to an Echo header plus the addresses. `null`: well formed but not an echo. Errors: `Truncated`, `UnknownIpVersion`, `BadHeaderLength`, `BadCode`, `TooManyExtensionHeaders`. |
| `parseIcmpEcho(family, icmp_message)` | The same from the ICMP type octet on, for a caller that walked the IP header itself. |
| `IpEcho.direction()` | `a_to_b` when `src` sorts below `dst`, `b_to_a` above; for `src == dst` (self-ping) requests are `a_to_b`, replies `b_to_a`. |
| `Estimator.observeEcho(EchoObservation) ?RttSample` | The echo matching rule above. |
| `RttSample.proto`, `.echoIdentifier()`, `.echoSequence()` | `Proto` is `tcp_timestamps` (default), `icmp_echo` or `icmpv6_echo`; for echo samples `tsval` holds the key. |
| `matchEchoReply(same, opp, cfg, obs)` | The echo core on two bare `TsTable`s, as `matchEcho` is for TCP. |

Out-of-order `now` values cannot crash the estimator: aging uses a saturating
age calculation, so they degrade to "nothing evicted" rather than UB.

## Verify

```
scripts/modtest pping                          # Debug       — 80 pass
scripts/modtest pping -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe   # ReleaseSafe — 80 pass
```

The option parser has a KAT corpus plus a hostile-input test proving it never
reads out of bounds. The table is tested for insert / lookup / remove / aging /
capacity eviction and for bounded memory under a long stream. The matching core
is pinned by the property harness: duplicate and delayed echoes must produce
**no** second sample, and a bounded table must not invent one. The echo decoder
has header-walk tests for every branch, a 20k-trial hostile-input test and a
`testing.fuzz` harness; the echo pipeline runs on real `ping` captures (see
Anchoring) and on scenarios for duplicates, unmatched replies, out-of-order
replies, cross-pinging hosts, table pressure, aging and refused mixing.

Provenance: the passive-RTT technique (match a TCP TSecr back to the TSval
that produced it, seen earlier in the opposite direction) and its
first-echo-match-and-consume rule are Kathleen Nichols' *pping* (Pollere LLC,
<https://github.com/pollere/pping>, **GPL-2.0-or-later**: `LICENSE` is the GPL v2 text, file headers say "version 2 … or any later") — ALGORITHM AND
BEHAVIOR ONLY, described in its public documentation and papers, studied as a
**design reference only**. No pping source was consulted, read or ported: this
module is an independent Zig implementation of a published measurement technique
(a technique is not a copyrightable work), and it deliberately shares no code
with, and derives nothing from, that GPL codebase. The wire format is RFC 7323,
a public spec. Echo matching by identifier and sequence is RFC 792 / RFC 4443's
own stated purpose for those fields; that xdp-project's pping (GPL-2.0-or-later)
also measures ICMP echo is known from its README only — none of its source was
read. DATA: the IPv4 echo frames in `src/echo_kat.zig` are real packets captured
from iputils `ping` with `tools/capture_icmp_echo.sh`; the IPv6 ones are built by
`tools/icmpv6_crosscheck.py` and checked with `tcpdump -vv`. The scenarios in `src/kat.zig` are hand-built `Observation` sequences with hand-computed expected `RttSample`s, written for this module. Nothing is taken from Pollere's pping, which was studied as a technique only; there is no vendored corpus.

## Backlog / deferred

- **Multi-flow table, flow events, output formats** (survey 2026-09-30, re-assessed 2026-10-06): xdp pping ships them; here the caller demultiplexes to one `Estimator` per flow, by design. A bounded flow map keyed by 5-tuple / address pair would save every caller writing one. Effort S–M. Fits §2.
- **A real ICMPv6 capture** (2026-10-06): the kernel the IPv4 goldens were captured on has no IPv6, so the ICMPv6 packets are self-built and tcpdump-checked. Re-run `tools/capture_icmp_echo.sh` on a host with IPv6; it records the `ping -6` run automatically.
- **QUIC spin-bit RTT** (survey 2026-09-30): Spindump does; TCP timestamps are optional and QUIC is a growing share of traffic, so this is where the technique goes next. Effort M. Fits §2. Only one unmaintained project ships it, so "nobody does this well" is possible.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle MIXED

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle MIXED** — anchored for some paths, self for others — the evidence below names which.

**What the tests actually contain.** src/parse.zig:207-224 anchors the TCP Timestamps option parser on 2 real SYN/SYN-ACK captures taken with tcpdump off a genuine loopback handshake, including the tsecr<-tsval echo. Everything above the parser is NOT anchored today: match.matchEcho is implemented (`gate.fable_core_implemented` in src/gate.zig, a switch left from when the core was a stub, is `true`), so the 8 KATs in src/kat.zig run and assert; their expected RTT sequences are hand-built scenarios (our own values, not an external capture). ICMP echo (2026-10-06), src/echo_kat.zig: **EXTERNAL** for IPv4 — 10 real IP packets from iputils `ping` on loopback, captured by tcpdump with nanosecond timestamps (`tools/capture_icmp_echo.sh`), including a real 65535 -> 0 sequence wrap; the expected RTTs are the capture-timestamp differences, each checked to be positive and no larger than the `time=` ping printed. **SELF-DERIVED** for IPv6 — six packets built by `tools/icmpv6_crosscheck.py`, decoded by `tcpdump -vv` with "[icmp6 sum ok]", made-up timestamps — and for the echo scenarios.

**How it got there.** The anchoring work landed. DONE a326e4a: real SYN/SYN-ACK timestamp options, tsecr<-tsval correlation anchored
